fusion_ranked_evidence.title: India’s Cockroach protests: Rahul Gandhi detained after calling for PM Modi to resign - The Guardian
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: Opposition leader taken away after accusing Narendra Modi of ‘destroying the future of India’s youth’ during protest in solidarity with cockroach movement. Indian police briefly detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday during protests calling for prime minister Narendra Modi’s resignation, in solidarity with the new youth-led cockroach party movement. Gandhi, the leader of India’s Congress party, staged a sit-in outside Modi’s house on Tuesday afternoon, stating that Modi must resign “for destroying the future of India’s youth”. His protest took place as thousands of students were gathered at a separate site in central Delhi, the day after a huge protest calling for the resignation of Modi’s education minister was met with brutality by Delhi police, including baton attacks and teargas. Gandhi said his party was taking their protest directly to the prime minister’s house, after the Modi government refused to take up the issues of the students and the alleged “brutality unleashed on students” in parliament.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: India’s youth-led Cockroach movement vows to keep demanding reforms after police crackdown - Greenwich Time
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # India’s youth-led Cockroach movement vows to keep demanding reforms after police crackdown. NEW DELHI (AP) — Supporters of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement demanding educational reforms and government accountability refused to leave their New Delhi protest site Tuesday, a day after their thousands-strong march toward Parliament drew police tear gas, beatings and a new wave of sympathy from across the country. The movement, now attracting professionals and families beyond students, represents a rare public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s government, reviving criticism over its handling of dissent and use of force to respond to protests. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and dozens of his Congress party lawmakers showed their support Tuesday with a sit-in outside Modi’s residence before police forcibly removed them in a dramatic escalation. Government minister Jitendra Singh said Gandhi was told the location was not “suitable for a sit-in.". Ada's coffee and candy shop on course to reopen in Riverside part of Greenwich.

fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Trump turns to 'zombie' court after Boasberg pointed to it in deportation fight - Fox News
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: The Justice Department filed its first-ever application for a removal order with the court on July 15, marking the first attempt in the court's nearly 30-year history to invoke a little-known law allowing the government to deport noncitizens suspected of terrorism through a specialized judicial process that relies on sealed classified evidence. "This Department of Justice will use every tool available to bring alien terrorists to justice and remove them from the United States, including by use of this court established by Congress in 1996," a Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement to Fox News Digital. The move also comes months after Chief U.S. District Judge James Boasberg in Washington, D.C., pointed to the long-dormant Alien Terrorist Removal Court as an alternative for handling terrorism-related deportation cases while questioning the Trump administration's use of the Alien Enemies Act.
